thread:
laura: FYI scanner caught a medium->high vuln in libssl in a few internal images. Looks like some images have a mismatched provenance (SBOM says openssl 1.1.1g but distro is 1.1.1k). Need rebuild + provenance fix.
sam: mismatched SBOM -> could be stale layer reuse in our build cache. Which images affected?
laura: list: staging/web:2026-03-11, test/worker:2026-03-09. SBOM excerpt:
```
name: openssl
version: 1.1.1g
layer: sha256:abcd1234
manager: apt
```
laura: but file /usr/lib/ssl/openssl shows 1.1.1k in the actual container runtime.
rachel: That's bad for attestations. If we sign these images they'll have wrong metadata. We should rebuild with cache-bust, produce fresh SBOM, and re-attest. Also restrict who can sign.
oz: Agreed. Proposal: create ephemeral signer key 'prov-rebuild-4309' in KMS, grant only ci-rebuilder-sa the AsymmetricSign permission for 1 hour, require OIDC token for the runner. Post sign events to security-audit sink.
sam: Minimal IAM JSON (will post in PR):
```json
{"bindings": [{"role": "roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier","members": ["serviceAccount:ci-rebuilder@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"],"condition": {"title": "temp","expression": "request.time < timestamp(\"2026-04-12T12:30:00Z\")"}}]}
```
sam: We'll also add storage.objectCreator for staging-registry and logging.logWriter.
laura: CI change: add build arg --no-cache and run sbom-generator step, then cosign attest using KMS. ci-bot, can you stamp the build with BUILD_ID and TRIGGERED_BY env so we have traceability?
ci-bot: [CI] build-#1204 started by laura -> no-cache true, sbom step enabled. Waiting for kms sign step.
rachel: Audit filters we need to wire:
- KMS sign filter:
```
resource.type="kms_key"
protoPayload.methodName:"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricSign"
protoPayload.request.name:"projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/prov-kr/cryptoKeys/prov-rebuild-4309"
```
- Registry push filter: match storage.objects.create to staging-registry bucket.
laura: Also add registry-level denylist support: if we detect a mismatch between SBOM and layers, auto-quarantine the image and block promotion. Rachel, can you add a quick lookup script to the runbook?
rachel: On it. Pseudocode in runbook: fetch SBOM, verify layer digests vs runtime files, if mismatch -> tag image quarantine:<digest> and post incident to incidents channel.
oz: Emergency revoke plan: if signer key compromised -> disable key, revoke IAM binding, invalidate OIDC tokens, add blacklist entry for any images signed with that key. Keep revoke script in the runbook.
sam: One more operational note: some old runners still use long-lived SA keys. We must ensure the job uses workload identity federation/OIDC; I'll add a hard check in the pipeline to fail if service account key file detected.
laura: Timeline: sam will create KMS subkey and short IAM binding in 15m, CI will start rebuilds, cosign attest and post attest id here, then we'll run a small canary to staging.
ci-bot: [CI] cosign: attestation created -> attest:sha256:ccddee3344 (signed with kms:prov-rebuild-4309)
laura: attestation id received. Running canary. Will report back with security smoke results.
rachel: Thanks. After canary, open PR to update base image Dockerfile with explicit package pin and add SBOM generation to default pipeline.
sam: I'll also add the audit-log alert to security-alerts channel with link to this thread.
laura: Closing loop for now. If anyone sees weird KMS activity, @oz please escalate. :lock:
